invariant-interval-identity-e0c992a8.title: Invariant Spacetime Interval
invariant-interval-identity-e0c992a8.interpretation: The invariant interval represents the absolute separation between events in 4D spacetime. It defines the 'metric distance' in Minkowski geometry, remaining constant for all inertial observers regardless of their relative velocity.
invariant-interval-identity-e0c992a8.symmetry_origin: This identity is a direct consequence of the Principle of Relativity and the constancy of light speed. It characterizes the manifold as Pseudo-Riemannian, where temporal and spatial coordinates contribute to the distance with different weights.
invariant-interval-identity-e0c992a8.limits_and_boundary: For \( ds^2 > 0 \), the interval is timelike (causally connected); for \( ds^2 < 0 \), it is spacelike (disconnected); and for \( ds^2 = 0 \), it is null (lightlike). In General Relativity, this flat metric is replaced by the dynamic metric tensor \( g_{\mu\nu} \).
